inspiration: The tool's viewers are one form per content type (mob, NPC, pet, mount, chair, effect ring, soul effect, damage skin, cash effect). That is a useful pattern for our own asset browser: one small viewer per asset family, with the same frame and playback controls.

Map scenery is animated with a skeleton runtime (Spine) and a particle system. Our own version could drive ambient props with a skeleton and add a small particle layer for dust, embers or spores. Use our own rig and art.
The particle emitter randomises start and end colour, size, spin, position and angle inside variance ranges. This is a clean, data-driven emitter layout to recreate with our own numbers and colours.
Floating damage numbers are picked from named 'skins' (style packs), and the viewer swaps them at runtime. Recreate as skinnable number styles with our own typography and colour logic.

Tooltip panels are built from separate corner and edge pieces (nw, n, ne, s, sw, se and others) rather than one bitmap. This is a nine-slice style frame worth recreating with our own ornament and palette.

A frame-list drawer (FrameListDraw.cs, name only, not opened) suggests the viewers step through frame lists per sprite set. Keeping the frame-list idea is fine; the sprites themselves are not usable here.

briefs.label: Segmented panel frame
briefs.why: A framed panel that scales to any size without stretching its ornament. Keeps menus readable and gives a consistent look across windows.
briefs.keep: Corners and edges as separate pieces; muted parchment-style base; thin inner rule
briefs.change: Our own ornament (asymmetric corner caps); a different palette; a notched border instead of a plain edge
briefs.ref: MapleNecrocer/Client/ToolTip.cs (around lines 26-30 and 64-83); read only, not opened further

briefs.label: Drifting ambient motes
briefs.why: Cheap living backdrop that makes a map feel lived in. Random variance on size and spin keeps it from looking repeated.
briefs.keep: Start and end colour ranges; slow fall with variance; short life per particle
briefs.change: Our own motion curve (sway or orbit instead of straight fall); our own colours and shapes; per-zone palette

briefs.label: Skinnable hit numbers
briefs.why: Players read damage at a glance and enjoy swapping styles. A named style list keeps the feature data-driven.
briefs.keep: Named style packs chosen at runtime; one loader for all styles
briefs.change: Our own typography and colour rules (crit and miss shapes); per-class number themes
